title: Destiny — Politics
text:
Title: Destiny — Politics

Metaphorical expressions of a predetermined destiny are commonly used by politicians to describe events not understood. Otto Von Bismarck said that the best a politician can do is to 'listen for God's footsteps and hang on to His coat tails'. General José de San Martín, Libertador of Argentina, Chile and Peru, famously said "You will be what you must be, or you will be nothing". In War and Peace, Leo Tolstoy wrote of the 'unconscious swarm-life of mankind', while Shakespeare spoke of a 'tide in the affairs of men' in his play Julius Caesar.
